subject: Tailored availability annex + order form language clarification (WellPath)
messages:
From: Priya Shah <contracts@wellpath.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Chu <procurement@wellpath.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Availability annex request + order form language (WellPath deployment)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we start the procurement loop I need to capture WellPath's required uptime and latency commitments in an annex to the MSA and specific order form language for the production deployment. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to the following (or propose alternate language):

- 99.95% monthly availability (regional) with a P95 latency target of <=200ms for text-generation requests under the committed throughput profile.
- A clearly defined maintenance window carve-out (we prefer 2 hours/month but can be flexible).
- Evidence package on go-live: operational runbook, failover test results (regional), and 90 days of latency/availability metrics.
- A credit schedule for downtime (monthly uptime < threshold -> credits on next invoice).

We will also need an order form that references the annex and confirms the dedicated capacity pool size, burst allowance, and model selections. I attached WellPath_SLA_requirements.pdf which includes our legal team's preferred credit bands and audit evidence checklist.

Ben (procurement) and I are hoping to close contract terms within the next 3 weeks. Can you please: 1) propose draft annex wording, 2) confirm what evidence you can deliver on onboarding, and 3) flag any items that require an exception or internal sign-off?

Thanks,

Priya Shah
Sr. Procurement Manager, WellPath Health
attachments: WellPath_SLA_requirements.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <contracts@wellpath.com>
Cc: Ben Chu <procurement@wellpath.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability annex request + order form language (WellPath deployment)

Priya — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Looping in Grace (ops) and David (legal/customer success) so we can respond with precise annex language and an evidence list.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- Grace will produce a technical annex draft (uptime/latency SLOs, maintenance carve-outs, and evidence matrix).
- David will review for order-form wording that ties the annex into the MSA and the DocuSign flow.
- I'll prepare a draft order form (shows committed capacity, burst allowances, and credit schedule) and share a DocuSign preview.

Two immediate clarifications from our side before we draft:
1) When you say "committed throughput profile", can you confirm expected RPS and peak burst RPS for the first 90 days? That will affect our latency guarantees.
2) Are you expecting regional (per-region) uptime guarantees or account-wide aggregated uptime? We typically offer region-level targets for dedicated pools.

We attached a working proposal (Redwood_proposal_v1.docx) that includes a sample credit schedule and a suggested 2-hr maintenance window language. We'll revise based on your answers.

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_proposal_v1.docx

From: Ben Chu <procurement@wellpath.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <contracts@wellpath.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability annex request + order form language (WellPath deployment)

Karthik / Grace —

Quick answers from procurement to help size the proposal:
- Expected steady-state: 30 req/s (text generation), anticipated bursts up to 120 req/s for up to 10 minutes during peak windows.
- We need per-region SLAs for our primary US-east and US-west deployments.
- Evidence: our auditors need a documented failover test plan and a one-time run during onboarding showing regional failover <5 minutes (time to route). They also asked for 90 days rolling retention for latency/availability dashboards (or nightly exports to an S3 bucket).

I attached the network/topology diagram we operate for the service boundary. We want the annex to specify where WellPath's telemetry will be collected and the format for the exported metrics.

Thanks — Ben
attachments: WellPath_network_topology.png

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <contracts@wellpath.com>, Ben Chu <procurement@wellpath.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 14:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability annex request + order form language (WellPath deployment)

Hi Priya / Ben — thanks for the details, helpful. Below is a first-pass technical annex snippet and an evidence matrix. I'm pasting plain text to make redlines easier; we'll provide as an attachment and a tracked-change Word file if you prefer.

----- BEGIN DRAFT UPTIME ANNEX (excerpts) -----
Redwood Inference Availability Annex (WellPath Health)
1. Scope: This annex applies to the Dedicated Capacity Order referenced in the Redwood MSA (Order ##). It covers availability and latency SLOs for the customer-specific deployment in the US-east and US-west regions.
2. Availability Target: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide 99.95% monthly availability per-region for production endpoints covered by the Order. Availability is measured at the model endpoint ingress for the committed capacity pool.
3. Latency Target: Redwood will aim to maintain P95 end-to-end latency <= 200ms for text-generation requests under the committed throughput profile (30 req/s steady-state; burst to 120 req/s up to 10 minutes). 
4. Maintenance Windows: Customer acknowledges a recurring maintenance window of up to 2 hours per 30-day period during which maintenance activities that may impact availability may occur. Redwood will provide at least 72 hours' notice for scheduled maintenance.
5. Credits: Monthly uptime below 99.95% will be eligible for service credits per the schedule in the attached Order Form. Credits are the customer's sole and exclusive remedy for availability outages and do not constitute waiver of other remedies in extreme cases.
6. Evidence & Audit: Upon go-live Redwood will deliver: a) onboarding runbook, b) regional failover test report (execution and results), c) access to 90 days of availability/latency metrics via nightly S3 export or shared dashboard link, and d) event logs for incidents required for claims. Redwood will provide SOC2 report on request under NDA.
----- END DRAFT UPTIME ANNEX -----

Attachments: uptime_annex_redwood_draft.txt

Notes / flags:
- The per-region phrasing is standard; if WellPath requires account-aggregated availability we need to route for legal approval since that changes the credit math.
- We can provide the nightly S3 export as requested; ops will require a signed data-transfer playbook to confirm retention and access scope.
- For the 5-minute failover target you mentioned, we can commit to test results on our side; real-world RTO is bounded by DNS and client routing and may vary. We recommend specifying "demonstrated failover completion within X minutes during the agreed failover test" rather than an unconditional guarantee.

I will slot internal ops time to run a lab failover and record the report once we have a provisional Order Form.

Cheers,

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
attachments: uptime_annex_redwood_draft.txt

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <contracts@wellpath.com>, Ben Chu <procurement@wellpath.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability annex request + order form language (WellPath deployment)

Priya / Ben —

Thanks — the draft annex and the clarifications look good to us. Next steps I propose:

1) We will attach Grace's draft annex to the Order Form and populate the committed capacity fields (30 req/s steady, 120 req/s burst) in the order.
2) David will drop in a clause that ties the annex to the Order and the MSA and clarifies that credits are the exclusive remedy for availability per the attached schedule.
3) Ops (Grace) will run and record the first failover test during onboarding and provide the report; we'll deliver the nightly S3 export for 90 days as requested.
4) I'll start a DocuSign flow for an Order Form preview — please review and redline the annex and order-form language once you receive the DocuSign packet. Link will also include the proposed credit schedule and a single-sheet "evidence checklist."

Proposed timing: I can get the DocuSign packet out by end of day tomorrow if that timeline works. If you can review within 4 business days, we should be able to finalize language and complete signatures within three weeks.

DocuSign preview: https://docusign.com/EXAMPLE-ORDERFORM-12345
Drive (drafts): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_draft

Please advise if any of the draft phrasing below needs to be stronger or if you'd like an alternative credit schedule. Happy to set a 30-minute call to walk the annex line-by-line.

Thanks — looking forward to closing.

Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_proposal_v1.docx
